400.description:
Bad Request (`InvalidDataError` / `ValidationError`).
    These occur when the request data is malformed or violates business rules:
*   `"Invalid payload, expected a json object"`
*   `"Require platform_id or platform_name"`
*   `"Invalid platform: {platform_id}"`
*   `"Cannot create more than {MAX_WAITING_JOBS} jobs"` (Global or offer-specific limit)
*   `"Max duration must not be zero"` or `"Max duration too large, exceeding 864000"`
*   `"Max_duration {value}(s) exceeds the platform limit of {limit}(s)"`
*   `"Invalid max_shots, should be a positive number"`
*   `"Max shots must less than or equal to {shots_limit}"`
*   `"Create job disabled, Platform in {status} status"` (e.g., decommissioned or retired)
*   `"Command '{command}' is not available on platform '{platform_name}'"`
*   `"Quantum Toolbox command '{command}' is not defined"`
*   `"Invalid iterator: must be a non-empty list"`
*   `"process_id is existed and assigned to another user job"`

401.description:
Unauthorized (`AuthenticationError`)
    Returned when the `Cloud Job Token` is invalid or there are account issues:
*   `"Invalid or expired job token"`
*   `"Authentication failed: explorer tokens are not allowed"` (If specifically restricted)
*   `"Invalid user"` (Returned if the user account associated with the token is deactivated)
*   **Credit/Time Issues:**
    *   `"Not enough credits"`
    *   `"Not enough credits: all remaining credits are reserved by waiting or running jobs"`
    *   `"Not enough {platform_type} time left"` (For Enterprise offers)

403.description:
Permission denied. 
    Returned when the user has a valid token but is restricted from this specific action:
*   `"Cannot have more than {MAX_QT_JOBS} running Quantum Toolbox jobs"`
*   `"No permission to use platform {platform_name}"`
*   `"No permission to use algorithm {command}"`
*   `"Platform {name} is locked, please upgrade your offer to use it"`

      <title>Ascella is back !</title>
      <link>https://account.quandela.com</link>
      <description><p>Dear photonic community,</p><p>Good news: maintenance is complete, and starting today Ascella, our 6-photon QPU, is available again to all users on Quandela Hub's cloud. Thank you for your patience while it was offline.</p><p><strong>New to Ascella?</strong> :</p><ul><li>6 photons</li><li>A 12-mode universal, fully reconfigurable photonic chip</li><li>Threshold single-photon detectors</li></ul><p>For the full picture (architecture, benchmarks and example applications), read the Ascella paper, <i>A general-purpose single-photon-based quantum computing platform</i>: <a class="ck-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00874">https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00874</a>.&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Getting started</strong></p><p>Set <code>"qpu:ascella"</code> as your remote processor in Perceval or MerLin, and you're ready to submit jobs.</p><p>We can't wait to see what you run on it.</p><p>Happy computing,<br>The Quandela team</p></description>

Your experimental workloads and feedback are crucial to our quantum evolution. Log in today, select Belenos from your dashboard, and join the vanguard of quantum innovation.</p><p>Share your experiences through our feedback portal – your insights will directly shape the future of practical quantum computing.</p><h2>Ascella Maintenance: Preparing for Its Next Evolution</h2><p>Our trusted 6-qubit Ascella processor will undergo scheduled maintenance beginning April 2025. Don’t worry – this temporary pause allows our team to implement radical enhancements to Ascella’s architecture.</p><p>Mark your calendars: Ascella returns by month’s end with heightened performance, improved reliability, and exciting new features designed to complement Belenos. All your existing configurations will remain intact.</p><h2>Two Processors, Infinite Possibilities</h2><p>Belenos and Ascella form the cornerstone of our quantum ecosystem, each serving distinct but complementary roles:</p><ul><li><strong>Belenos:</strong> Our powerhouse for pushing quantum boundaries and tackling the most demanding computational challenges</li><li><strong>Ascella:</strong> Our optimized platform ideal for specific workloads, education, and applications requiring its unique characteristics</li></ul><p>Together, they create an unparalleled quantum computing environment that outpaces anything currently available. Whether you’re revolutionizing financial modeling, accelerating drug discovery, or solving impossible optimization problems, our dual-processor approach ensures you’ll have the perfect quantum tool for every task.</p><h2>The Future is Quantum, and It’s Here Today</h2><p>The quantum future we’ve all been waiting for has arrived. Belenos represents not just an impressive technological achievement, but a practical quantum computing resource that delivers real-world value today.</p><p>Begin your quantum journey with Belenos now, and prepare for an enhanced Ascella experience soon. Together, we’re not just witnessing the future of computing – we’re creating it.</p><p><strong>Access Belenos today and transform the impossible into the inevitable!</strong></p></description>

qpu:ascella

QPU Ascella is one of our online quantum computers. It features 12 available modes and up to 6 photons. With Ascella, you can implement any unitary transform on 12 modes -- it is universal. A schematic of the chip is shown above.

The detectors are not number-resolving (i.e. cannot differentiate between 1- and n-photon states).

Depending on your algorithm, you may be interested in the n-photon coincidence rate. You can calculate it as Clock [MHz] x (Transmittance)^n.

The QPU supports sampling commands: samples and sample_count.

For more information about the Quandela Cloud and how to get started, refer to the Documentation. Information about using Perceval to interact with our cloud computers is available here. And if you have any questions, send us a message by clicking the Support button in the bottom right of any Cloud page.

parameters.use_photon_recycling: Legacy - Use the mitigation setter instead - boolean enabling the Photon Recycling noise mitigation process. Replaces default mitigation if no user-defined mitigation is given, else it is ignored (Default False)

qpu:belenos

QPU Belenos is our online quantum computer. It features 24 available modes and up to 12 photons. Belenos chip architecture is universal, meaning any unitary transform can be implemented. A schematic of the chip is shown above.

Some of the detectors are quasi number-resolving (i.e. they can differentiate between 1- and n-photon states).

Depending on your algorithm, you may be interested in the n-photon coincidence rate. You can calculate it as Clock [MHz] x (Transmittance x Brightness)^n.

For more information about the Quandela Cloud and how to get started, refer to the Documentation. Information about using Perceval to interact with our cloud computers is available here. And if you have any questions, send us a message by clicking the Support button in the bottom right of any Cloud page.

sim:ascella

SIM Ascella is one of our online QPU simulators. It can simulate up to 6 photons in 12 modes, assuming both perfect and imperfect sources, so that you can estimate the performance of your QPU jobs. A schematics of the simulated chip is shown above. To be consistent with the QPU's threshold detectors, detectors simulated as threshold too.

SLOS is used as computation back-end, which allows you to fully characterize an output distribution without the need for sampling individual shots.

The simulator natively supports sampling commands: samples and sample_count.

For more information about the Quandela Cloud and how to get started, refer to the Documentation. Information about using Perceval to interact with our cloud computers is available here. And if you have any questions, send us a message by clicking the Support button in the bottom right of any Cloud page.

sim:sampling

A Clifford & Clifford 2017 based simulator which allows you to run simulations using between 2 and 12 photons, with computational power supported by OVHcloud. It uses the Clifford & Clifford algorithm to produce provably correct random samples from a particular quantum mechanical distribution, with a time complexity of n1.8^n for dual-rail encoding. See: https://perceval.quandela.net/docs/backends.html .

The simulator supports all available commands interchangeably: samples, sample_count and probs.

The simulator computes ideal as well as noisy computations and supports post-selection and heralding.

For more information about the Quandela Cloud and how to get started, refer to the Documentation . Information about using Perceval to interact with our cloud computers is available0 here. And if you have any questions, send us a message by clicking the Support button in the bottom right of any Cloud page.
